## Why This Is Asked

MERGE INTO iceberg.target AS t
USING staging AS s
ON t.id = s.id

WHEN NOT MATCHED THEN INSERT (id, field, updated_at) VALUES (s.id, s.field, s.updated_at);
```

# PySpark-like pseudocode (simplified)
df = spark.readStream.format("json").load("/events")
staged = df.selectExpr("event_id", "region", "payload.*")
staged.createOrReplaceTempView("staging")

spark.sql("""

USING staging AS s

""")
```

## Architecture
- **Ingestion**: Apache Kafka with 3 partitions, replication factor 3
- **Processing**: Apache Flink for windowed aggregations and joins with exactly-once semantics
- **Storage**: Raw events in S3 (Parquet format), processed data in Redshift

## Data Quality & Schema Evolution
- Schema validation using Confluent Schema Registry
- Data quality checks with Great Expectations
- Dead letter queue for failed events
- Debezium CDC for reliable change data capture

## Why This Is Asked

It also compares light-weight pandas vs distributed Spark choices and requires a minimal test plan. It emphasizes practical constraints like maintainable contracts and observability.

- Batch ingest

## Code Example

```python
# Minimal PySpark skeleton
from pyspark.sql import SparkSession
from pyspark.sql.functions import col

spark = SparkSession.builder.appName("event_pipeline").getOrCreate()

# Read and validate
df = spark.read.json("s3://bucket/events/*.jsonl.gz")
valid_df = df.filter(
    col("user_id").isNotNull() & (col("user_id") != "") &
    col("event_type").isin(["login", "view", "click"]) &
    col("created_at").isNotNull()
)

# Flatten attributes
from pyspark.sql.functions import from_json, schema_of_json
attr_schema = "map<string,string>"
valid_df = valid_df.withColumn("attributes_flat", from_json(col("attributes"), attr_schema))

# Write conforming data
valid_df.write.partitionBy("event_date").parquet("s3://lake/events/")

# Route bad data
bad_df = df.subtract(valid_df)
bad_df.write.parquet("s3://lake/bad_events/")
```
